subject: Payment API throughput drop - SLA remediation request
messages:
From: Marta Ruiz <marta@clearlinepay.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Thomas Nguyen <thomas@clearlinepay.com>
Date: Thu, 21 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Payment API throughput drop - SLA remediation request

Hi Logan,

We saw a sustained drop in payment authorizations through your /v1/pay endpoint between 2028-06-21T02:45:00Z and 2028-06-21T03:20:00Z (approx). Our payments queue backed up, orders failed, and we incurred chargebacks during that window. Per our contract (SLA section 4.2), we would like Redwood to confirm the outage window, provide any available evidence, and advise on credit eligibility and timeline for a postmortem.

Attached is our local client-side trace and a sample of failing request IDs. We need:
- Confirmation of the impacted interval in your systems (start/end)
- Any mitigations you applied (routing/failover)
- ETA for an internal postmortem and when we can expect a remediation credit estimate

This is time-sensitive — our finance team is preparing a customer-facing report. Please loop in anyone who needs to help verify timings.

Thanks,
Marta Ruiz
Head of Platform Ops | Clearline Payments

Attachments: clearline_client_trace_0621.jsonl (client traces), failing-request-ids.txt
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta@clearlinepay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 21 Jun 2028 09:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Payment API throughput drop - SLA remediation request

Hi Marta — thanks for the report and the trace bundle. I'm escalating this to our SRE/incident team. Quick summary of what we'll do next:

1) We'll validate the service-level telemetry (ingress rates, 5xx/429 spikes, autoscaler events) and confirm the impacted window.
2) Ben will pull runtime traces and an aggregated log bundle; Marissa will coordinate any credits/contract questions.
3) We'll aim to share an initial impact window and a runbook of mitigations within 24 hours, and a preliminary credit estimate within 3 business days.

Could you also confirm whether you observed elevated client retries or a sudden surge of concurrent requests at 02:40–02:50Z? That helps us distinguish service-side degradation vs client-side saturation.

I'll follow up once we have the verified window.

—Logan
Logan Wright
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1-415-555-0142

Hi all,

I pulled the runtime metrics and log slices for 2028-06-21 02:30:00–03:40:00Z. Preliminary findings:

- We observed a cluster-wide upsurge in tail latencies starting ~02:41:12Z with 5xx and 429s peaking at 02:48:00Z.
- Autoscaler performed a scale-up at 02:49:30Z; pods came back into service by 02:56:00Z.
- There was a transient metadata service error for shard assignment between 02:43:00Z–02:47:00Z which increased queueing on the inference frontends.

I've attached a compressed log bundle and a trimmed JSONL of sampled runtime traces (runtimetraffic-logs-20280621.tar.gz, clearline_trace_20280621.jsonl). Those include internal correlation IDs that match the request IDs you sent.

Next steps:
- Formalize the impacted window as 02:41:12Z–02:56:00Z pending a coordinated trace reconciliation with your client traces.
- We'll run the postmortem to verify root cause (we suspect a control-plane metadata glitch during shard rebalance).
- Marissa, can you prepare a provisional credit calc based on the SLO table (we'll use the defined 99.9% availability formula)?

Ben Carter
SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: runtimetraffic-logs-20280621.tar.gz, clearline_trace_20280621.jsonl
